title: Term lock: one name per concept across abstract, demo and code
outcome: A glossary that fixes one public name per concept so the abstract, diagram, demo and contracts never use two words for one thing
acceptance: Covers at least: envelope, read/write set, gateway, recorder, witness, verify, lineage hold, graded containment (suspend/revoke/release), taint-scoped revert, re-run vs replan, root candidates, oracle S*, R and C, TTI-detect/attribute, TTC
Each entry: locked term, one-line plain-English gloss a banking reader understands, banned synonyms, and matching code/contract identifier where one exists
Maya confirms every code identifier matches contracts C1-C6 (or flags the mismatch)
summary: abstract/TERMS.md: ~65 locked terms in 6 tables (actors/path, record/audit, classes+containment, recovery, metrics, demo). Each row: locked term, gloss <=15 words for a banking reader, code name from C1-C6/module list, banned synonyms. All acceptance terms covered. Key locks: 'suspend' (not quarantine), 'lineage hold', 'record' (not log), 'taint-scoped revert', 're-run' vs 're-plan', 'root candidates' (not culprit/root cause), 'kill switch' = project name only; R/C metric-vs-class overload rule. Sec 7 lists 9 contract gaps for maya: revert vs C5 'restore'; Alert.suspect vs culprit; no contract for provenance graph, witness checkpoint, side store, hold window/sensitive tag, metric field names, idempotency_key; Control.target must accept a connection id (D7); reconcile detector name.
